main_body: White porcelain bathtub: a rim ring around a light-blue water opening, with a white and grey front face and two small gold feet
top_band: Rows 2-3 white back rim, rows 4-9 water opening (dark blue back edge, then light blue), row 10 white front rim; about 8 rows of horizontal surface in total
evidence: In the middle column, rows 0-1 are the dark outline. Rows 2-3 are the white back rim. Rows 4-9 show the water surface, a darker blue back edge fading to light blue with a highlight, which reads as an interior seen from above. Row 10 is a bright front rim line, rows 11-13 are the white-to-grey front face, and row 14 holds the feet. The opening is a clear 6-row interior between the rims, so it is a real 3/4 container and not a rim-only drawing or a flat slab.

style.evidence: The tub has about 4 tones on the white and grey body and 3-4 blues in the water. The water is a large flat light-blue block with only a small highlight and a darker top edge. The white rim and front are smooth fills with no grain or speckle. The outline is a neutral dark grey with almost no tint, which gives a sticker look. Most tiles carry only 2-4 colours, well below the stall and well references, which have tile scallops, stone-by-stone shading and wood grain.
